verdict.rationale: Sentry documents its own OTLP ingestion of OpenTelemetry traces and logs, either directly from an OTel SDK or through the OpenTelemetry Collector. Code instrumented with open-standard OTel can therefore target Sentry, or move away from it, without re-instrumentation. Only traces and logs are documented, so the open-standards path covers part of the telemetry surface. Missing for 10: OTLP metrics ingestion, documentation of feature parity for OTel-sourced data versus Sentry's own SDKs, and independent or hands-on corroboration of backend switching via OTel.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can instrument once with open standards and switch backends without re-instrumenting my code

citations.quote: Sentry can ingest OpenTelemetry traces and logs via OTLP endpoints, either directly from an OTel SDK or through a pipeline tool like the OpenTelemetry Collector.
